**Continuous 2.10.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.10.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.10.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.10.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.10.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.10.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.10.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.10.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.10.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.10.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.10.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.10.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.8.2

**Security hardening.** A batch of fixes from an outside review, merged as #419 to #437. The ones you may notice:

- **A cloned folder's configuration needs your trust.** MCP servers, models, providers, data destinations and repo-root rc files that arrive with a folder are held back, with secrets and saved MCP sign-ins withheld, until you trust the folder. VS Code asks with a dialog; in the CLI use `cn project trust` or `--trust-project-config`. Your own configuration wins any name collision. (#430)
- **Permission checks fail closed.** A command too long to read in full asks instead of passing; an edit waits for you when the rules cannot be checked; a headless run keeps deny rules, floor rules and protected paths; MCP tools are covered by `mcp__server__*` floor rules; the Agents window and experimental retrieval follow the same rules. (#426, #427)
- **Loop workers inherit your policy.** A worker used to start in auto mode. It now runs under the parent's flags and levels and cannot ask, so something that needs a question fails the item. A loop at a cautious level may stop on a command that used to run unattended. (#426)
- **Loop checks run where your commands run.** A check goes through the same executor as the Bash tool (including WSL and the container), a refused or denied check fails the item instead of marking it done, and a check that times out stops the process it started. Loop-wide token and time limits are enforced during an item. (#419)
- **The CLI no longer loads a project `.env`** into its own process. `~/.continuous/.env` is still read. (#425)
- **`cn serve` and the binary dev port check who is calling.** Host and Origin are checked; a bearer token is checked when you set one with `--token` or `CONTINUOUS_SERVE_TOKEN`. On loopback the token is optional; off loopback the server will not start without one of 16 characters or more. (#423, #438)
- MCP app tool calls follow tool policy (#421); fetch, proxy redirects, docs crawling and the Chromium download are hardened (#424); the VS Code webview and the JetBrains panel are hardened (#428); restore, apply and provider conversion paths (#431) and path resolution for protected files (#433) are tightened; the release workflows pin their actions and checksums (#422).
- Provider and loop reliability: cost, stream, cache and listing bugs (#420), atomic session saves and a stricter `POST /message` (#419), tool-call parsing, IPC framing and next-edit fixes (#436).

**Where commands run**

- **WSL fails closed and says how to fix it.** Where 2.8.1 added running commands in WSL, a missing WSL or distribution now means the command is not run and you are shown `wsl --install`; it never falls back to PowerShell. Where commands run is now one place in core, so the IDE and the terminal agent share it. (#410)
- **Run commands in a container.** `continuous.terminal.shell: container` runs each command in a fresh Docker or Podman container: the workspace folder only, no network, no capabilities, a read-only image, your user. `continuous.terminal.containerRuntime` and `containerImage` pick the runtime and image. With no runtime installed, or its daemon stopped, commands are not run and a notice says how to fix it. (#416, #434)

**Rules for where a command talks to**

- **`host:` and `net:` rules.** A deny or ask rule can name a destination (`host:*.aliyuncs.com`, `net:metadata` for cloud metadata addresses), read from the arguments of `curl`, `wget`, `git`, `ssh`, `scp`, `rsync`, `nc` and a few more, with decimal, hex and octal IPs normalised. A destination built by an interpreter or a variable is not seen. (#415)

**Loop budgets**

- **Set a budget.** The budget controls are hidden until you choose **Set a budget...** on the plan card: a strategy (equal, weighted by size, fair share), a reserve, and a number per to-do in tokens, minutes or turns, with a proposal from the loop's finished work. Each task row shows its runs, tokens and time, and what is left of its budget. (#412, #413, #439)
- **A budget line in the plan.** `budget:` under a to-do. An item that reaches its limit ends as over budget with its work kept. (#417)
- **What happens at the limit** follows your policy: Suggest asks (Extend, Split, Skip, Block), Force ends the item and lets the loop's strategy continue, Review allows one extension from the reserve for an item that is making progress. Extensions come from the loop's reserve, so the loop's total stays a ceiling. The CLI keeps ending the item over budget. (#439)
- **Held questions select, then apply.** Choose an answer, then press Answer. (#412)
- Dollar budgets are not enforced yet.

**Underneath**

- The stuck-agent signals (repeat calls, ping-pong, edit and revert, no progress) and a work log exist as tested functions with adapters for CLI and IDE histories and a measurement script; nothing in the product uses them yet. (#414, #435)

**Planning**

- The roadmap records what is built and not built for each of these. See [`plans/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/plans/ROADMAP.md).

## Not included

The JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continuous. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
